sources: dossier=Net position (2026-05-12 nomenclature-resolution; 2026-05-19 crimefinder, artifact) explicitly lists blob bytes under byte-opaque inertness, not structural; doc=inertness.md line 18 (byte-opaque applies-to) already listed blob content correctly, but §21 (line 34) called blob content structurally inert, contradicting both line 18 and the dossier; code=node_attributes.go rehydrates spilled blob bytes for substitution walks, consistent with byte-opaque's substitution-leaf read site
note: Doc self-contradicted on blob classification. The dossier resolves the contradiction in the opposite direction from the row's own hypothesis: line 18 (byte-opaque) was already correct, and it was §21 (line 34) that mis-classified blob content as structurally inert. Fixed §21 to split blob content (byte-opaque) from executor error payloads (structural, unchanged).

sources: dossier=silent on the specific enumeration but Required Behaviors line 16 sanctions claim-content read sites narrowly (walkPath only, no other path); doc=claim-scope.md Boundaries ('Owns: the conflict-check comparison ... inertness discipline at all rimsky-side sites') and Invariants (byte-equal conflict predicate, scopes-conflict RPC delegation) name the conflict comparison as a legitimate rimsky-side read the exclusive inertness.md line-18 enumeration denied; code=lineage_writer.go HashBytes(ClaimScope) and conflict.go byte-equality corroborate
note: claim-scope.md (adjacent, second-precedence design corpus) claims ownership of the conflict-check comparison as a sanctioned read site; inertness.md's 'only at substitution-leaf extraction or for transport' enumeration was exclusive and omitted it. Fixed line 18 to add the byte-equality conflict comparison as a named sanctioned site.

sources: dossier=Required Behaviors 'Subscription topic filters operate only on metadata ... never payload bytes' (2026-05-14, artifact-only) describes topic/type-path matching, a distinct field from the payload predicate and not contradicted by this ruling; doc=node-subscription.md ('declares a target signal ... plus an optional payload predicate') and attribute.md ('subscribers can predicate over payload.attributes_delta via CEL') both current-state corpus docs sanction a CEL payload predicate spanning the signal payload; code=signal/cel.go CompileWhenWithBodyFields validates payload/error_payload field refs
note: The dossier's 'topic filters ... metadata only' line concerns type-path/topic selection, a separate field from node-subscription's 'optional payload predicate' — no real conflict, dossier is simply silent on the payload-predicate mechanism. Two adjacent, current design-corpus docs plus code confirm the CEL payload predicate is a designed, sanctioned read site spanning message and error payloads that inertness.md's 'pattern-match prohibition still binds' sentence denied. Fixed line 19 to name this site.

sources: dossier=the uniform-prohibition bullet (2026-05-11 log-convergence; 2026-05-17 post-data-platform-cleanup, artifact) lists logged/%v-formatted/validated/transformed/traced/error-included as prohibited but does NOT include 'hashed' -- a corroborating omission; doc=lineage-record.md Invariants ('held-claim references carry the claim-scope-data hash, not the bytes themselves ... Per the inertness discipline, inert bytes do not appear in lineage records') sanctions hashing as the inertness-preserving mechanism; code=lineage_writer.go HashCanonicalJSON(AttributesMerged)
note: The dossier's own prohibition list omits hashing, and the adjacent lineage-record concept explicitly frames a value hash as the mechanism that keeps inert bytes OUT of a derived record -- i.e. hashing is inertness-compliant, not a violation. Fixed line 19's flat prohibition to drop 'hashes' from the blanket ban and add a narrow, named exception for a downstream owning concept's derived-record hash.

sources: dossier=Required Behaviors line 18 'Message payload bytes are inert: read only via {{trigger.message.payload.<path>}} walkPath substitution ... and the GET /messages/{id} fetch' does not deny a delivery-time bag population, and 'body_schema serves registration-time substitution-ref checking; actual validation happens ... when a receiver pulls values at dispatch' implies dispatch reads the body; doc=message.md Invariants ('populates the run's attribute bag from the message body') directly confirms delivery reads the payload; code=message_delivery.go::deliverNamedMessageInTx calls messagePayloadAsMap then Upsert/SetDispatchInputBag
note: message.md's own Invariants section (adjacent, second-precedence corpus, current-state) states delivery populates the receiver's attribute bag from the message body -- directly contradicting inertness.md §24's claim that delivery 'touches envelope routing fields ... but never the payload.' Fixed §24 to describe the delivery-time bag population as a sanctioned structural-inertness read, matching message.md.

sources: dossier=silent on this specific sentence; doc=inertness.md's own §18/§21/§24 name substitution-leaf verbatim extraction and executor-wire transport as sanctioned sites, neither of which is an equality predicate, directly contradicting the generalizing sentence at line 37
note: Internal self-contradiction verified directly from the doc's own content: the generalized claim that 'each read site evaluates equality predicates on attribute paths only' is false for the doc's own enumerated substitution-leaf, conflict-comparison, and executor-wire sites. Rewrote line 37 to describe the actual variety of read shapes (verbatim extraction, equality comparison, wire transport) instead of overgeneralizing to equality-only.

sources: dossier=Corrections/Required Behaviors line 29 'Audit records store request_params verbatim (not hashed) -- justified because control-plane request bodies never carry secrets; the API key travels in the Authorization header and is never stored' (2026-05-15, control-plane-mcp-and-auth, artifact-only); doc=inertness.md line 41 claimed this guarantee follows from 'rimsky's structural-inertness discipline' itself
note: The dossier confirms the underlying policy (verbatim storage, API key is the only treated-as-sensitive value) almost verbatim, but frames it as a deliberate control-plane policy choice, not a logical consequence of inertness (inertness governs rimsky's own inspection, not what data a consumer puts in a body). Reworded line 41 to state the dossier's actual justification instead of over-claiming a guarantee inertness does not provide. Not design-incoherent, so ruled directly rather than as design-call despite the artifact-only tier.

sources: dossier=Net position places blob bytes under byte-opaque inertness (2026-05-12; 2026-05-19 crimefinder, artifact); doc=inertness.md line 18 vs §21 (line 34) self-contradiction, plus blob-backend.md's own read-site list ('substitution path-walk leaf and ... persistence-layer fetch on read') disagreeing with line 18's generic 'transport into the executor's wire' phrasing for blob content
note: Same underlying defect as row 66 (blob classification self-contradiction) plus the adjacent-doc read-site mismatch with blob-backend.md. Same edit resolves both: §21 now classifies blob content byte-opaque, and line 18's byte-opaque read-site list now names blob-spill movement between column and backend (matching blob-backend.md) instead of the generic 'executor's wire' phrasing that never applied to blobs.

sources: dossier=silent on the specific enumeration, does not contradict; doc=claim-scope.md Boundaries and Invariants name the conflict-check comparison and the scopes-conflict RPC delegation as owned, sanctioned rimsky-side reads of claim-scope bytes; code=conflict.go byte-equality, runner_acquire_claims.go/peer/client.go ScopesConflict RPC transport
note: Same underlying defect as row 67 (claim-scope conflict-predicate read site omitted from the byte-opaque enumeration). Same edit to line 18 resolves both by adding the byte-equality conflict comparison as a named sanctioned site.

sources: dossier=silent on the literal phrasing; doc=attribute.md's substitution grammar names claim payload fields as a path-walking source kind with an optional-empty trailing path, which requires walking the claim payload's JSON structure to resolve a nested leaf, contradicting the doc's own 'never traverses the bytes at all' at the very read site it names two sentences later
note: Self-contradiction on the doc's own terms: 'never traverses at all' is immediately followed by a substitution-leaf site that, per attribute.md's path-walking source-kind grammar, does traverse JSON structure to reach a nested field. Softened the byte-opaque bullet's opening sentence to describe interpretive opacity (never assigns meaning to the bytes) rather than an absolute no-traversal claim that the doc's own sanctioned site violates.

sources: dossier=n/a (a doc-hygiene rule, not an intent question); doc=inertness.md line 19's 'gained ... described below' uses change-over-time phrasing barred by the design-doc current-state-only rule, and no later section in the doc names or describes a 'shared matcher evaluator'
note: Verified directly: the current-state-only rule bars 'gained' framing, and grepping the rest of the doc confirms no section actually describes the matcher evaluator, so 'described below' dangled. Rewrote the sentence in present tense and inlined a one-clause description of the matcher evaluator's primitive-equality read site in place of the dangling forward reference.

sources: dossier=n/a (a doc-completeness question, not an intent question); doc=inertness.md line 14 names message payloads and scratch (per concept:executor) as governed streams, and both concept:message and concept:executor exist as concept docs, but the Boundaries Adjacent list at line 27 omitted both
note: Verified directly against the doc's own governed-stream list and the existence of both target concept docs. Added concept:message and concept:executor to the Adjacent list.

sources: dossier=Required Behaviors line 18 cites 'the GET /messages/{id} fetch' as the sanctioned persistence read, silent on list endpoints; doc=message.md line 31 is terser ('the persistence-layer fetch') and does not itself claim single-row-only, so inertness.md's added 'a single message row' specificity was the doc's own overreach; code=messages.go handleListMessages surfaces payload per row, substitution_context.go lists all delivered messages for a frame
note: inertness.md §24 added a 'single message row' qualifier that neither the dossier nor the adjacent message.md concept doc supports, and that code contradicts (list endpoint and frame-wide substitution-dep listing both surface payload across multiple rows). Broadened §24's persistence-fetch clause to 'message rows (single or list)'.

sources: dossier=Superseded/historical: 'Historical numbered labels (invariants 11, 20, 21, 24) -- the numbering scheme itself was later banned from source and diagnostics ... the disciplines the numbers named remain in force under descriptive names' (2026-06-19, a02fe167, transcript); doc=sensor.md, publisher.md, publisher-subscription.md all cite 'invariant: message-inertness' with no matching name in inertness.md's §24 (numbered-only); message.md independently cites 'invariant: 21' for message payload (a further, different mismatch, out of scope for this file)
note: Transcript-tier intent establishes descriptive naming as the current convention, corroborated by three sibling docs already using 'message-inertness'. Added the '(message-inertness)' name to §24 so the cross-doc citation resolves. A full repo-wide sweep to drop §-numbering (and to reconcile message.md's own conflicting 'invariant: 21' citation) would require editing claim-scope.md, blob-backend.md, and message.md, which are out of scope for this edit -- flagged for a follow-up plan rather than done here.
